question: With BLOWER and EXTRACT in AUTO, what avionics ventilation configuration is used on the ground before take-off power is set (normal skin temperature)?

options.text: Overboard extract with the blower stopped

explanation: On the ground before take-off power the system runs open circuit, drawing air in and sending it overboard.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: On the ground before take-off power, when does the avionics ventilation use the closed circuit instead of the open circuit?

options.text: When the skin temperature is below the ground threshold
When the cabin doors are closed

explanation: A cold skin can cool the recirculated air on its own, so there is no need to take outside air.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: With both switches in AUTO, what configuration is used after take-off power is applied and in flight?
explanation: In flight the cold skin cools the recirculated avionics air, so the closed circuit is used.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What happens when either the BLOWER or the EXTRACT pushbutton is set to OVRD?

options.text: Both fans stop and the system goes open circuit
The system goes to closed circuit and air from the air conditioning system is added to the ventilation air
The avionics are cooled only by the skin heat exchanger

explanation: OVRD on one switch brings conditioned air into the closed avionics circuit.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What happens to the blower fan when the BLOWER pushbutton is set to OVRD?
explanation: With BLOWER in OVRD the blower fan stops and conditioned air takes its place.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: With both BLOWER and EXTRACT set to OVRD, how does the ventilation air flow?

options.text: Round the closed circuit only, with both fans stopped
From the cargo compartment into the cabin
From outside through the skin inlet and back overboard
From the air conditioning system, through the avionics, and then overboard, with the extract fan still running

explanation: This is the configuration used for avionics smoke: conditioned air in, straight out overboard.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Which of the following does NOT turn on the BLOWER FAULT light?

options.text: Loss of power to the ventilation computer

explanation: BLOWER FAULT comes from low blowing pressure, duct overheat, computer power failure or the smoke warning.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: Which of the following turns on the EXTRACT FAULT light?
explanation: EXTRACT FAULT comes from low extract pressure, computer power failure or the smoke warning.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When the avionics smoke warning is active, what do the BLOWER and EXTRACT pushbuttons show?

options.text: Nothing; smoke is shown only on the ECAM

explanation: The smoke warning lights both FAULT lights, prompting the crew to set them to OVRD in the procedure.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: How many cabin (recirculation) fans does the CAB FANS pushbutton control?
explanation: CAB FANS ON runs both cabin fans; OFF stops both.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: How are the cargo compartments ventilated?

options.text: A dedicated pack supplies conditioned air
Ram air flows through them in flight
An extraction fan draws air out of the compartment and overboard, and cabin air flows in to replace it

explanation: The extract fan creates the flow; the supply is cabin air.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: With the AFT ISOL VALVE pushbutton in AUTO, when does the cargo extraction fan run?

options.text: When no smoke is detected in the aft cargo compartment
Only when the cargo doors are closed
Only when HOT AIR is ON

explanation: In AUTO the inlet and outlet isolation valves open and the fan runs unless smoke is detected.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What does setting the AFT ISOL VALVE pushbutton OFF close?

options.text: The inlet and outlet isolation valves and the cargo trim air valve, and the extraction fan stops

explanation: OFF isolates the compartment completely, including the hot trim air used for cargo heating.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: What turns on the AFT ISOL VALVE FAULT light?

options.text: An inlet or outlet isolation valve not in the selected position

explanation: FAULT is a valve disagreement, with an ECAM caution.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: When is VENT shown in amber on the PRESS page?

options.text: When there is a BLOWER FAULT, an EXTRACT FAULT or an AVNCS SYS FAULT
When the cabin fans are off
When the outflow valve is open

explanation: Avionics ventilation is displayed on the PRESS page, below the cabin pressure data.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.

question: On the PRESS page, what does an amber XX on the avionics inlet or extract valve mean?

options.text: The valve position is unavailable or the data are inconsistent

explanation: XX is always 'no valid data' on the ECAM.
reference: Study use only. Verify against the FCOM of your operator and aircraft before relying on it.
